task.description: Implement lib/letflow/design/req029-node-attribute-edge-condition-validators.md's design in lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex: validate_node_attributes/1, validate_edge_conditions/1, and valid_cel_syntax?/1, plus every private check_* helper and the ISO-8601 duration parser the design specifies. This extends the existing merged module in place -- do not create a new file. No migrations needed (pure functions, no DB).
acceptance_criteria: each of the 7 node types has at least one explicit test: HUMAN_TASK missing role, SERVICE_TASK missing endpoint, SERVICE_TASK invalid timeout (0 and >300000), TIMER missing/invalid duration, TIMER P0D explicitly accepted, and START/END/gateway types accepting no attributes
an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge with both a non-null condition and is_default: true is rejected
an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY with two edges both marked is_default: true is rejected
isValidCelSyntax-equivalent rejects at least one structurally invalid expression and accepts at least one structurally valid one, with an explicit test noting it performs no evaluation
extra undeclared attributes on a node do not cause a violation, demonstrated by an explicit test
no Repo/Logger/DateTime.utc_now/File/HTTP call anywhere in the new code (purity contract, same as REQ-028)

result.summary: Extended lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex in place per the approved design doc, exactly as specified -- no new file, no struct changes, REQ-028's validate_graph/1 and CHK-01..08 untouched. Added: (1) validate_node_attributes/1 (public) running CHK-09..12 (check_human_task_role/1, check_service_task_endpoint/1, check_service_task_timeout/1, check_timer_duration/1) via the same unconditional flat_map-and-concatenate composition as validate_graph/1; (2) validate_edge_conditions/1 (public) running CHK-13..17 (check_gateway_condition_presence/1, check_non_gateway_condition_absence/1, check_default_condition_conflict/1, check_single_default_edge/1, check_cel_syntax/1), reusing the existing private build_node_index/1 helper to resolve each edge's source node type, with a dangling source defensively treated as 'not a gateway' rather than raising; (3) valid_cel_syntax?/1 (public) -- bracket/string-literal balance scan via Enum.reduce_while plus a bare-leading/trailing-operator check; (4) the private ISO-8601 duration scan-forward parser (valid_iso8601_duration?/1 + scan_duration_tokens/2,3) per design doc §4.3. Violation.code type extended with the 9 new atoms (missing_role, missing_endpoint, invalid_timeout, invalid_duration, missing_edge_condition, unexpected_edge_condition, default_with_condition, multiple_default_edges, invalid_cel_syntax). Moduledoc extended with an 'Ordering contract' paragraph per design doc §1, stating that neither new function calls validate_graph/1 or verifies structural validity, and that enforcing 'PD-05/PD-06 run only after validate_graph/1 succeeds' is the caller's job (REQ-030's future create/1). Node.attributes reads are string-keyed only (Map.get(attributes, "role") etc, per design doc §2's atom-exhaustion-avoidance pin) with is_map/1 guards so every new helper stays total/defensive (never raises) even on an unexpected attributes shape. Design doc §9.1's flagged reconstruction gap (ISO-8601 parser and CEL syntax algorithm, both reconstructed from requirements.yaml prose since R-Co source is unreachable on this host) surfaced no new ambiguity during implementation -- the design's own algorithm description (scan-forward token matching against an ordered, no-repeat unit list; a reduce_while bracket/string-literal scanner; first/last-token bare-operator rejection) was concrete enough to implement directly. I did not silently trust the reconstruction: after mix compile/format passed, I ran a throwaway `mix run` sanity script (not committed) against every worked example the design doc itself gives in §4.3 and §6 -- 5 valid + 7 invalid ISO-8601 durations, 3 valid + 3 invalid CEL strings, plus AC1 (timeout 0/300000/300001 boundaries), AC2 (gateway edge with is_default:true and a condition -> exactly 2 violations, unexpected_edge_condition + default_with_condition, matching the design's explicit 'these two co-fire' note), AC3 (2 default edges on one gateway -> exactly 1 violation on the 2nd), AC5 (extra undeclared attribute keys -> valid: true), and START/END/gateway nodes with nil attributes (-> valid: true). Every result matched the design doc's stated expectation exactly; no divergence found, so nothing needed flagging to REVIEWER on this point. Verification commands run: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> 'Compiling 1 file (.ex) / Generated letflow app', exit 0. `mix format --check-formatted` initially failed on 5 long-line spots (all inside the new code); ran `mix format lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex`, then `mix format --check-formatted` exited 0 clean. Purity grep `grep -n "Repo\.\|Logger\.\|DateTime\.\|System\.os_time\|HTTPoison\|Req\.\|File\." lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex` returned exactly one hit -- the moduledoc's own prose line ('no HTTP/file call'), not executable code -- so zero real matches, purity contract holds. `mix test test/letflow/definitions/graph_test.exs` -> '15 tests, 0 failures' (REQ-028's existing suite is unaffected by the in-place extension). Self-review checklist from the role file: no Repo/Logger/DateTime/File/HTTP calls in the new code (confirmed above); every new public function (validate_node_attributes/1, validate_edge_conditions/1, valid_cel_syntax?/1) has a one-line @doc; no existing call site's signature changed (validate_graph/1 untouched), so nothing else to recompile-check; this doesn't touch process_instance.ex/instance_supervisor.ex so no state-diagram/crash-isolation re-check applies; no migration added.
